newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel says cabinet to call for strong mark, euro.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says cabinet to call for strong mark, euro.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Tuesday that the German cabinet would make a statement calling for a strong euro and a strong mark after its meeting on Wednesday.
"Tomorrow we will say that we are for a strong euro and for a strong mark," Waigel told Reuters on the sidelines of a European prize-giving ceremony in the Bavarian town of Dillingen.

Speaking earlier in Berlin, Waigel said Germany was interested in a strong mark, that markets had overreacted in pushing the dollar and sterling to multiple-year highs, and suggested that the Group of Seven (G7) could be prepared to take corrective action.

Waigel's support for the mark came hot on the heels of similar statements from Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer last week, but failed to hold the dollar back as it soared to 71-month highs above 1.80 marks.

Analysts blamed the mark's weakness on a simmering row in Germany over how strictly entry criteria for European economic and monetary union (EMU) should be interpreted. They said this had discredited both the planned euro and the mark.

The G7 industrialised nations, which in 1995 called for an "orderly reversal" of the dollar from record lows near 1.3450 marks, signalled in February at a dollar rate of about 1.65 marks that the recovery had gone about far enough.
